terms.definition: The electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions in a lattice.
terms.examiner: "Electrostatic attraction" and "oppositely charged ions" are the marks.
A single covalent bond is one shared pair.

terms.definition: A shared pair of electrons in which both electrons are supplied by one atom.
terms.examiner: Shown by an arrow from the atom that donates the lone pair.

terms.definition: The attraction between delocalised electrons and positive ions arranged in a lattice.
terms.examiner: Refer to delocalised electrons, not "free" electrons, and to a lattice.

terms.definition: The power of an atom to attract the pair of electrons in a covalent bond.
terms.examiner: A difference in electronegativity between two bonded atoms gives a polar bond.

terms.definition: Induced dipole–dipole forces: a temporary dipole in one molecule induces a dipole in a neighbouring molecule.
terms.examiner: Present between all molecules; stronger with more electrons and a larger surface area.

terms.definition: The attraction between a δ+ hydrogen bonded to N, O or F and a lone pair on N, O or F in another molecule.
terms.examiner: Diagrams need the partial charges, all the lone pairs and the bond drawn from the lone pair to the hydrogen.

terms.definition: Pairs of electrons around a central atom repel each other and get as far apart as possible; lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs.
terms.examiner: State the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs before naming the shape and the bond angle.
